items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized 1889 at Larrow Green, main creamery 1891, Gideon Vose first president.
Gives pay by butterfat test not weight, but never states the second bolded element, that the test of the station where he delivers governs.
Story 1: the provision 'made every later dispute a matter of money rather than opinion'.
Only Hobart Sill is named as buttermaker in Section A. Effie Loomis is absent and Teague is not identified as bookkeeper in A.

Stories 1 and 8: Selby Vose is Gideon's son, not nephew, and manager. The year is not given in A. The core fact is credited under the key's rule for items with more than two bolded elements and no REQUIRED line. The 1911 in B3 is deducted separately.
Story 7: the ledger's 'station gain' line, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual', carried to the general account, with more fat arriving than was credited.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
No account in A of the weighing, composite sample, percent-graduated neck or fixed pipette charge.
Story 1: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897.
Story 1: six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 2: 'a flat deficiency of 0.19 points, present in every season alike, not just winter'.
A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie was tester from the 1896 opening for 29 seasons and was dismissed on 30 April 1925.
Only 'test book' is bolded. Story 4 has 'the station's own test book (in Keddie's hand)'. The description is thin but meets the bolded gate.
Neither summary-leaf figure appears in A: no 1896 average of 3.80 and no 3.61 from 1898.
Story 3: broken 8 May, borrowed measure until 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back, question mark in the book. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the core fact is present.
Stories 5 and 8: married Orra Brant, Emmet Brant's sister, and Emmet was the station's largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he 'tested as he was taught and cannot say why' is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died 1934 under the imputation. Test book impounded 1925 and sent to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom's six farms, wet meadow, Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Scales agreeing is stated, but the bolded start date of 1 January 1897 for the weigh book is missing.

Story 2 gives the visible gap as 0.19 ('tested lower than the rest of the valley: a flat deficiency of 0.19 points'), and C1b equates the 3.80 true figure with Larrow Green's 3.78. That conflates the 0.17 visible gap with the 0.19 shortfall, which loses the item under its gate.
Grigg's 1908 committee is named in A, but the January-March 1908 sampling is not. It appears only in E20.
A has no 1910 figures (200,000 lb at 3.42) and no statement that the loss was proportional.
A has the weigh book lent to Ivy in 1958 but never says it passed to Roy Brant or that he lent it. Both bolded elements are required.
Jerome Cudd as founder and Redlow Ridge are missing from A. Vessey County appears only as the book's later repository.
Story 7: 'the four Hessel Bottom farmers who hauled there in summer'. The year 1915 is missing, but the core fact is present.
The Alder Corners test is not stated as independent on two of the four elements (county, bench, glassware, uncompared book). Only the artifact is named.
Gives 3.78-3.82 'no different from anywhere else' but never the ~0.19 higher than Ostrey Hollow over sixteen seasons, 1915-1930.
A never argues that the same milk tested differently in two buildings, defeating hay and watering together.
Rosalie Cudd is named and the book is 'copied for Ivy 1958', but A never says she was Jerome's daughter or that sixteen seasons were copied.
The inspector's lactometer visits are dated 'from 1908 on' (NT-23). The key has 1907-1936.
The lactometer 'found no added water at any circuit visit' at the station.
A has neither the 12 June 1923 date nor the burette run and condemnation. It says only 'condemned ... 1923'.
A never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency.
A has no replacement-glass dates and no 1924 average of 3.80. F1 elsewhere asserts 3.85, which is deducted.
Story 8: crate in the loft 1923-1958. Strawn notebooks to the state office 1936 and the Farland college library 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Story 4: petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, sessions partly in the station's weigh room.
Stories 2 and 4: watering (Vose), theft by the tester, and bog hay were all argued, and 'no cause established' for any.
The four exhibits are listed, but A never says Strawn's 1923 notebook contained the answer and was read for its other lines. That clause is bolded.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the award, no cause established; award $3,800 'without admission'. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
A has neither the one-fifth of $19,000 nor the charge to the account where the gain had accumulated. The fraction appears only in C.
Ivy Keddie, b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Story 7: separate records 'none connected ... only in combination, after 1958'. Story 8 traces each series into Ivy's hands.
Story 6: February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes survived.
Asserts a mean delivery of 16.27 c.c. (NT-1). The key has 16.72, 0.95 of the mark.
A never states that every test read 95 percent of true, with 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood.
A has none of the milk, fat, money or ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958 is present, but the bolded intervals (35, 33 and 24 years) are not stated in A.
Granddaughter, via Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father). Great-niece rejected using r22's correction and r18.
Second cousins, correctly derived (1). The full- vs half-sibling question (A08) is never raised (0). Not asserted either way, so no deduction.

Gideon Vose as father (1). Its significance is given as signing the ledger that undercut his accusation, not Article VII making the test decisive or the Vose Jerseys losing most (0). B3 also asserts manager 'from 1911', which is deducted.
Asserts 'no relationship' between the Voses and the Keddies (A01) rather than declaring it unsettleable. Takes -2.
Uses 16.27, giving a 7.6% shortfall. The key has 0.95, 5 percent.
Final answer 3.80, short 0.19. It gets there by 3.61+0.19, not by 3.61/0.95, but the stated values match.
Adds 0.19 to get a 3.61 true test, so 7,220 lb and 380 lb. The key has 3.60, 7,200 and 360 lb.
$95.00 (380 x 0.25). The key has $86.40, and the $90.00 exception does not apply.
76,000 lb, 5.26% of the credited fat with the denominator named, and 5.0% of the true total noted.
72 pipettes is right, but each is said to be short 1.33 c.c. The key has 0.88. Both are required.
Gives 'just over 26 years', not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks. The 25 full years and the reason are right, but all figures are required.
Reports 'approximately 1,100,000 lb' as the answer on Kyle's recollection, ignoring the conflicting 900,000, and never says it cannot be determined (A02). Takes -2.
Variable: the measuring glass, own broken and borrowed substitute used.
Same tester, same herds, same season, same procedure.
Nine weeks; tests rose and fell back the day the station glass was restored. No 3.80 or 3.61 figures, credited under the core-fact rule for items with more than two bolded elements.
Cause tracked the glassware, not tester, herds or feed. Limit stated: does not give the size of the deficiency or the mechanism.
Three reasons from different narrators: the 1911 interval (r22, r18, r24), Sill's 'ran heavy' (r14), Kyle's ledger station gain (r23).
Claims all three are independent, but Sill's 'ran heavy' and the ledger surplus rest on the same event (the cream's heavy arrival). The independence claim fails.
Answers 'No.' on Kyle's word that the bookkeeper never asked anybody (A09), a definite assertion. Takes -2.
Yes: he knew the station tested low, having publicly addressed it in the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five: signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Manager from 1911 is wrong, the 1926 address is not the 1925 hearing argument, and nothing on his never naming glass.
Asserts 'the sources indicate he did not know' that the ledger contradicted his explanation, on Kyle's testimony (A03). Takes -2.

Resolved with a method stated: invoice $77.93 against $77.39 (primary invoice); condemnation 12 June 1923 (official report); glass in use 1 May 1897 (two contemporaneous documents); the 1908 sampling (E20, report against covering letter). Capped at 3.

Pairs noticed and broken: NT-15 five dozen in r11 and r21, broken by the firm's own invoice; NT-18 great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by r22's own correction and r18; NT-10 1898 in r11 and r23, broken by r20's invoice and r24's diary. Capped at 3. NT-1 was broken the wrong way.
No abstention conflict (A04, A06, A10) is put in B-G as unsettleable with what the record establishes. A10's lost date is mentioned only in Section A. A04 is half-adopted ('mold likely reground').
Names r11's self-contradiction (the 118,000 body text against its 76,000 conclusion) and r15's 'whole of 1908' above a three-month report.
Cause given as pipettes delivering 16.27 c.c. (~7.6%), not 16.72 (95%). It never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80 and gives the 1924 average as 3.85.
Watering (Selby Vose), defeated by the inspector's lactometer never finding water.
Theft (Teague), defeated by the cream running heavy (Sill, the ledger station gain) and by the 1911 interval.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp), defeated by Bulletin 214's actual 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, against a flat year-round 0.19.

'No evidence that it did', then 'Oram independently corroborates the crate sat unexamined'. No declining qualifier, and the award's 'appliances' phrase and Frick's claim go unaddressed (A07). Treated as an assertion: -2.
'The sources conflict and this is not fully resolved ... I do not consider this fully settled.' It leans toward Duncan while explicitly declining, so this is a correct abstention.
About 148 words.
At most ledgers and the 1958 measurement among the nine record series. Diaries, circular, memoirs and bulletin are not the key's series.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
Has 1897, the 1923 inspection, 1958, and Ansel and Ivy named: four of six, covering both ends.

deductions.reason: Corruption: pipettes delivering 16.27 c.c. asserted as fact (F033), in Story 6, C1, C4 and F1
Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits from 1908 (NT-23), in Stories 2 and 5
Corruption: 1919 circular sent to eleven families (F058), in Story 5 and E13
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship asserted as 'no relationship' (B4)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as ~1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper asserted never to have questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: manager asserted not to have known of the understatement (D3)
Gullibility A07: board asserted not to have examined the glassware, crate 'sat unexamined' (F)
